body.text: The Reload published all weekend and handed this board two documents it did not have: a federal under-21 ruling nobody had carried, and a named explanation of the one thing that could still sink the NFA win.

On Friday 08/21, Judge George O'Toole (D. Mass., Clinton appointee) upheld Massachusetts' under-21 handgun and semi-auto possession ban in Escher v. Noble, rejecting an NRA-backed challenge on the founding-era "infancy doctrine." Two Reagan appointees have now reached opposite results on the identical federal statute — and ATF never appealed the loss.

facts.title: 1. ATF ransomware breach — second outlet, named reporter
2. Militia-clause amicus wave in Viramontes / Grant
3. Escher v. Noble — MA under-21 ban upheld

body.text:
• Escher v. Noble: MA under-21 semi-auto ban upheld on the infancy doctrine
• The threat to the NFA injunction is standing, not the merits (California v. Texas)
• ATF NFA processing fell to eight days in July — good for owners, awkward for the case
• Michigan Senate nominee declined 3x to disavow replacing the Second Amendment
